text: Keeping young chicks in proper housing reduces the major causes of chick mortality in villages — dogs, cats, wild animals, and motorbikes. Housing also improves welfare by keeping chicks in a dry environment protected from rain and wind, so they don't waste energy and become weak; ensures they get enough water and feed during the high-risk early growth period; makes vaccination practical, since scavenging poultry are hard to catch; and reduces disease risk by preventing contact with sick poultry and scavenging in rubbish where Salmonella and Pasteurella thrive.
